column3: The Hebrew wording names silence without explicitly naming rulers; BSB supplies O rulers.
The Hebrew has a singular heart; BSB has hearts.
The Hebrew repeats womb or belly imagery; BSB varies womb and birth.
The Hebrew explicitly says deaf and has a singular ear; BSB omits deaf and has ears.
The Hebrew first names charmers in the plural; BSB has a singular charmer.
The Hebrew names young lions; BSB says lions.
The Hebrew has a singular archer and cutting off arrows; BSB has plural archers and blunting arrows.
The Hebrew names a snail melting without a separate reference to slime; BSB supplies slime.
The Hebrew does not separately name dry; BSB interprets the contrast as green or dry.
The Hebrew has a singular righteous person seeing vengeance; BSB has plural people seeing they are avenged.
The Hebrew names a singular person speaking and fruit for the righteous; BSB has men and a reward.
